To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

exposure to repeated stress produces neuroadaptation in the basolaterial amygdala (a region that is important for fear and anxiety) that confers an enhanced capacity of amygdala neurons to produce and engage in short-term retrograde signaling mediated by endocannabinoids (a neuromodulatory system that regulates synaptic transmission).
repeated, but not a single exposure to restraint stress elevates 2-AG levels in the BLA and enhances 2-AG-dependent DSI.

exposure to repeated restraint stress produces neuroadaptation in the BLA, which enhances the capacity of BLA neurons to elevate 2-arachidonooylglycerol levels and engage in 1,2-diolein-mediated short-term retrograte synaptic signaling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neurobiological basis for stress-related psychiatric disorders such as post-traumatic stress disorder, depression and anxiety.
the role of endocannabinoids (eCBs) in stress-induced behavioral adaptations, with a focus on the basolateral nucleus of the amygdala (BA).
understanding how stress affects the brain, and the role of the endocannabinoid signaling system in mediating the effects of stress.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stress-induced enhancement of endocannabinoid-mediated suppression of inhibition in the BLA is associated with the increased 2-AG levels in BLA.
stress induces neuroadaptation in the basolaterl amygdala that enhances short term endocannabinoid signaling.
the stress-induced increase in the levels of 2-Aracydonoylglycerol in BLA could contribute in affective dysregulations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
repeated stress elevates 2-arachidonylglycerol (an endocannabinoid) and enhances short-term endocannabinoid signaling at inhibitory synapses in the basolater amygdala.
repeated stress produces a neuroadaptive change in the BLA that enhances the capacity to engage in short-term retrograde signaling via the eCB 22:0-2-AG.
chronic, but not acute stress, increases 2-AG synthesis, and enhances 2-AG-dependent suppression of inhibitory synaptic transmission in the basolater amygdala.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chronic stress causes neuroadaptations that enhance the ability of BLA neurons to synthesize and release the eCB  2-AG and engage in  2- AG-mediated short-term retrogradesynaptic signaling.
repeated stress causes a long-term adaptation in the endocannabinoid system that enhances the ability of neurons to engage in endocannabinoids-mediated synaptic plasticity.
chronic stress produces neuroadaptation that confers BLA neurons with a greater capacity to elevate  2-AG content  and engage in  2- AG mediated short-term retrograde signaling.
